After 8a31 the guard raises `McpEnvelopeError` (a RuntimeError with no `returncode`) as `ToolError.__cause__`; McpEnvelopeError is neither a ConcurrencyError nor carries returncode, so both assertions pass without exercising the intended not-found-vs-concurrency discrimination. The parallel `_concurrency_cause` helper (test_mcp.py:377) WAS updated to read `cause.envelope[...]` and `cause.__cause__`, but this negative-path test was left reading the old shape.

advisory.finding: test_mcp_rejection_identity_distinguishes_not_found was not updated for the new envelope wrapping; its cause is now an McpEnvelopeError, so its assertions (`not isinstance(cause, ConcurrencyError)`, `returncode != 10`) pass vacuously and no longer verify the docstring's claim that the chained cause is a plain RebarError (exit 1) discriminating not-found from concurrency.
advisory.suggested_fix: Read the McpEnvelopeError off __cause__, assert `cause.envelope["error"] == "ticket_not_found"` and `cause.envelope["exit_code"] == 1`, and assert the deeper `cause.__cause__` is a RebarError but not a ConcurrencyError.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the semantic repurposing of the public MCP `error` return key (prose -> code) is an intended, documented, and acceptable wire change for external agents.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:31 now emits `"error": "llm_unavailable", "message": str(exc)` where it previously emitted `"error": str(exc)` (per diff)
src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:84 `return {"error": code, "kind": exc.kind, "message": str(exc)}` — `error` was previously `str(exc)` prose

In-repo consumers grep: only tests reference these dicts' `error` key (tests/unit/test_llm_disposition_plumbing.py:165, tests/interfaces/contracts/test_mcp_error_envelope_heldout.py:254-265) — all updated; no production consumer reads `.error` as prose, so the break is external-only
advisory.finding: The public MCP tool return shapes for `_structured_llm_failure` (review_code/verify_completion/review_plan) and `explain_criterion` repurpose the existing `error` key from human prose (`str(exc)`) to a machine code, moving prose to a NEW `message` key. This is an unversioned semantic change to a public MCP return contract: an external agent that previously read `.error` as a human-readable string now gets a short code instead, with the prose relocated. In-repo consumers are only tests (all updated), so nothing breaks inside the repo, but the wire contract for out-of-repo agents silently diverges.
scenarios: An external MCP agent branching on the human text of `error` from review_code/verify_completion/review_plan/explain_criterion failures
